quests.protocolRule: What would show that someone was actually hurt?
quests.crisisScene: A spider has scared a child in the backyard, but no one has been bitten. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: COMFORT THE CHILD AND CHECK FOR A BITE, NO SERVICE NEEDED
quests.actionGuidance: Being frightened isn't the same as being hurt. Checking for a bite is enough, and no emergency service is needed.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Some swallowed objects are far more dangerous than they look.
quests.crisisScene: A toddler has swallowed a small button battery from a toy. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR MEDICAL HELP IMMEDIATELY
quests.actionGuidance: A button battery can cause serious internal injury within hours, so it needs urgent medical attention even without visible symptoms.

quests.protocolRule: What is the standard first-aid step, and what would make it worse?
quests.crisisScene: A teenager has a mild nosebleed after being hit by a ball during a game. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SIT HIM FORWARD AND PINCH HIS NOSE, CALL ONLY IF IT WON'T STOP
quests.actionGuidance: A mild nosebleed after a knock usually stops with pressure and leaning forward. Bleeding that won't stop would need help.

quests.protocolRule: Crush injuries need trained assessment.
quests.crisisScene: A warehouse worker has a forklift roll onto his foot and he can't move it. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR AN AMBULANCE AND KEEP HIS FOOT UNTOUCHED UNTIL CREWS ARRIVE
quests.actionGuidance: A crush injury can cause damage that isn't visible from outside, so paramedics need to check him.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what water near electricity can do.
quests.crisisScene: Heavy rain has flooded a basement and the water is rising near an electrical panel. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: EVACUATE AND CALL FOR HELP
quests.actionGuidance: Rising water near electrical equipment risks electrocution, so everyone should leave before help arrives.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what actually protects people right now.
quests.crisisScene: Hail the size of coins is falling and denting cars in an open parking lot. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET INDOORS, THIS DOESN'T NEED A SERVICE CALL
quests.actionGuidance: Taking shelter protects people immediately; large hail damaging property isn't itself a reason to call emergency services.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what number matters most here.
quests.crisisScene: A car has flipped on the highway and you can see two people trapped inside. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL THEM TWO PEOPLE ARE TRAPPED INSIDE
quests.actionGuidance: Knowing exactly how many people are trapped helps dispatch the right number of responders and equipment.

quests.protocolRule: Think about how many households this could affect.
quests.crisisScene: A gas leak is suspected in an apartment building with multiple units. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT HOW MANY UNITS MAY BE AFFECTED
quests.actionGuidance: Knowing how many units might be affected helps responders decide whether to evacuate the whole building.

quests.protocolRule: Think about why a count still matters, even without injuries.
quests.crisisScene: A minor bus accident has happened and everyone insists they feel fine. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE NUMBER OF PASSENGERS ANYWAY
quests.actionGuidance: Reporting the passenger count still matters, since some injuries take time to show and responders need to know the scale.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what happens if the ice breaks under a person too.
quests.crisisScene: A dog has fallen through thin ice on a pond and its owner wants to walk out to it. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR HELP, DO NOT WALK ONTO THE ICE
quests.actionGuidance: Ice that couldn't hold a dog likely can't hold a person either, so trained rescuers with the right equipment should go instead.

quests.protocolRule: Some dangers can't be seen just by looking at them.
quests.crisisScene: A power line has fallen across a driveway after a storm. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: STAY AWAY AND CALL FOR HELP
quests.actionGuidance: A downed line can be live even if it looks harmless, so staying well back keeps everyone safe until it's handled.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Think about what happens if the rescuer slips too.
quests.crisisScene: A hiker has slipped near the edge of a cliff trail and a friend wants to pull him up alone. Input rescue code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR RESCUE, DON'T ATTEMPT IT ALONE
quests.actionGuidance: An untrained rescue attempt near a cliff edge risks a second person falling, so trained rescue teams should respond instead.

quests.protocolRule: Ask why a driver would suddenly stop like this.
quests.crisisScene: A driver has stopped in the middle of a busy intersection and won't move, blocking traffic. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CHECK ON THE DRIVER, THIS MAY BE MEDICAL
quests.actionGuidance: An unexplained stop in traffic can be caused by a medical emergency, not just carelessness, so it should be checked as one.

quests.protocolRule: An alarm sounding is a reason to act on its own.
quests.crisisScene: Smoke alarms are going off in an apartment building but no smoke is visible from outside. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL THE FIRE BRIGADE TO CHECK
quests.actionGuidance: A sounding alarm should be treated as a real signal until firefighters confirm otherwise, even without visible smoke.

quests.protocolRule: Think about who should check it, not who should touch it.
quests.crisisScene: A shopper has left a bag unattended near the entrance of a crowded mall. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT TO SECURITY OR POLICE
quests.actionGuidance: Reporting an unattended bag lets trained staff assess it safely, without anyone approaching or moving it themselves.

quests.protocolRule: What would have to change for this to matter?
quests.crisisScene: A man says he has a mild headache after a long day at work. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REST AND FLUIDS, SEE A DOCTOR IF IT LASTS OR CHANGES
quests.actionGuidance: A mild, ordinary headache can usually be managed with rest and fluids, with a doctor's visit if it lasts or changes.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what makes this headache different from an ordinary one.
quests.crisisScene: A man has the worst headache of his life, appearing suddenly, along with blurred vision. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET AN AMBULANCE NOW AND NOTE WHEN THE HEADACHE STARTED
quests.actionGuidance: A sudden, severe headache with vision changes can signal a serious condition, so it needs immediate medical attention.

quests.protocolRule: How is he acting compared with how hot he is?
quests.crisisScene: A child has a low fever and is a little tired but still playing normally. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: KEEP HIM COMFORTABLE AND WATCH FOR LETHARGY OR BREATHING TROUBLE
quests.actionGuidance: A low fever with normal behavior usually doesn't need emergency care, unlike a fever with lethargy or breathing trouble.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what tells paramedics what to bring.
quests.crisisScene: A cyclist has been hit by a car and is conscious but can't move his leg. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL AN AMBULANCE AND SAY HE CAN'T MOVE HIS LEG
quests.actionGuidance: Mentioning he can't move his leg helps paramedics prepare for a possible fracture before they even arrive.

quests.protocolRule: Think about the fire and the injury as two separate needs.
quests.crisisScene: A fire has started in a kitchen and the cook has burns on both hands. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR FIRE AND MEDICAL HELP TOGETHER
quests.actionGuidance: This scene needs both firefighters for the fire and paramedics for the burns, so both should be requested together.

quests.protocolRule: Think about her injury and the danger to others separately.
quests.crisisScene: A woman has been bitten by a dog and the dog is still loose nearby. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR MEDICAL HELP AND REPORT THE LOOSE DOG
quests.actionGuidance: Reporting the loose dog protects others nearby, while requesting medical help treats her injury, so both need mentioning.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Ask what else this could be, besides sleep.
quests.crisisScene: A man is lying still near train tracks, and a bystander assumes he's just sleeping. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CHECK ON HIM, DON'T ASSUME HE'S SLEEPING
quests.actionGuidance: Assuming someone is 'just sleeping' near a hazard like train tracks could delay help he urgently needs.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what a loud argument could actually be.
quests.crisisScene: Neighbors hear shouting from next door and assume it's just a loud argument. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT, DON'T ASSUME IT'S HARMLESS
quests.actionGuidance: Shouting could signal a dangerous situation, so it's safer to report it than to assume it's harmless.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what hazard lights sometimes really mean.
quests.crisisScene: A driver sees a stopped car with its hazard lights on and assumes the driver is fine, just parked. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CHECK OR REPORT IT, DON'T ASSUME
quests.actionGuidance: Hazard lights can mean trouble, not just parking, so it's worth a quick check or a report rather than an assumption.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what waiting costs in this situation.
quests.crisisScene: A man says his symptoms 'will probably pass' during what looks like a stroke. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR AN AMBULANCE NOW, DON'T WAIT
quests.actionGuidance: Stroke symptoms need treatment within a narrow window, so waiting to see if they pass can cost precious time.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what a small spill could turn into if ignored.
quests.crisisScene: A worker hesitates to report a small chemical spill because he doesn't want to 'make a fuss'. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT RIGHT AWAY ANYWAY
quests.actionGuidance: A small spill reported immediately is far easier to manage than one that's allowed to spread while someone hesitates.

quests.protocolRule: Think about which mistake is worse: calling too soon or too late.
quests.crisisScene: A babysitter isn't sure if a child's allergic reaction is 'bad enough' to call for help. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR HELP NOW, DON'T WAIT TO BE SURE
quests.actionGuidance: Calling for help even when unsure is safer than waiting for certainty, since allergic reactions can worsen quickly.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what silence from a caller might mean.
quests.crisisScene: A man was talking normally when he called for help, but has now gone quiet on the line. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: STAY ON THE LINE AND TREAT THIS AS MORE URGENT
quests.actionGuidance: A caller going quiet suggests his condition may be worsening, so the situation should now be treated as more urgent.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what responders still need to know.
quests.crisisScene: A small kitchen fire that seemed under control has suddenly grown and started spreading to a cabinet. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: UPDATE THE FIRE BRIGADE ON THE CHANGE
quests.actionGuidance: Letting the fire brigade know it has grown helps them prepare with the right equipment before they even arrive.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what changed since the first call.
quests.crisisScene: A person reported as having a minor cut is now feeling dizzy and pale. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL THE AMBULANCE HE'S NOW GETTING WORSE
quests.actionGuidance: Reporting that he's getting worse helps paramedics arrive better prepared for a more serious situation than first described.
